QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_13

question.text: Initial margin in equity derivatives is designed to cover:

answer.text: The worst-case potential loss on a portfolio over a specified time horizon with 99% confidence (VaR approach)
The total contract value of all open positions
The brokerage and transaction charges for the trade
The profit expected to be earned from the derivative position

explanation.text: The Logic: SPAN identifies overall portfolio risk and sets initial margin to cover the largest reasonably expected one-day loss. Initial margin is based on the 99% Value at Risk (VaR) concept. Where next-day MTM settlement value may not be collected before the next-day trading begins (for futures contracts on index or individual securities), the source allows a two-day horizon in those conditional cases. The Trap: Initial margin is not the full contract value, nor is it linked to brokerage or expected profits. It is a risk-based number sized to cover a worst-case one-day portfolio loss at 99% confidence. Note: Source: NISM-Series-VIII workbook (Dec 2025), pages 160-161.
